[2026-07-07 20:29 CDT] Book-mining anti-drift gate (Proposal A — coverage accounting) · Plain: added the one missing safety net for book mining. Book mining already proves every claim it CAPTURES is well-formed (corpus_verify) and already has a full human end-audit (corpus_audit_gate), but nothing proved we captured EVERYTHING — so whole chapters/appendices/books got silently skipped (DDDL's Appendix-B long tail, Immortality sitting at 0 claims for ~40 sessions) and we only found out much later, forcing whole-book re-mines. This is the exact same "silent absence" class as the PreWorkout Pixie miss, at book scale. The new gate makes wholesale skips a RED board the moment a book is declared done, instead of an invisible dropped thread. It does NOT run book mining or change any claim — it's a small forcing-function tune-up so Phase G is safer when we get back to it; the product-extraction flow (resume at the U-range) is untouched. · Files: eden/tools/mining-coverage.json (NEW — per-book ledger: mining_status incomplete|complete, coverage_basis screenshot|section, reviewed_empty{page:reason}, sections[]); tools/invariants.py (NEW gate check_mining_coverage_accounted + registration, board 45->46). · How it works: for a book flagged mining_status:'complete', every source page (screenshot-scheme books) or section (chapter-scheme books) must be claim-bearing OR reviewed-empty-with-a-reason, else RED. Claim-bearing pages AUTO-DERIVE from sealed locator.char_offset -> nearest '===== Screenshot(N) =====' marker — ONE internally-consistent text-position basis (I verified locator.screenshot is populated inconsistently per book: epigenetics numbers by Page, iaiyh/immortality by marker N, so it's deliberately NOT used). 'incomplete' books (all 6 today) report an informational coverage snapshot and NEVER red the board — same design as book_source_clean asserting only pristine books, so the legitimately-incomplete corpus stays green. reviewed-empty reasons follow the exceptions_justified pattern. Scope: WHOLESALE accounting only; per-claim sub-page completeness stays with corpus_audit, faithfulness with the manual mining checkpoint (the 3-leg system: this gate + checkpoint command + end-audit). · Verifications: PYTHONUTF8=1 python tools/invariants.py -> 46/46 green; NEGATIVE TEST — flagged iaiyh mining_status:complete with 15 unresolved zero-claim pages -> gate RED with the exact page list (Screenshot [739,740,741,...]); restored -> green. Empirically validated the char_offset->marker derivation reproduces known page assignments (iaiyh 20/20, immortality 196/196) BEFORE building on it. The gate immediately surfaced the known under-mining: immortality 49/254 pages mined (205 zero-claim), epigenetics 66/465 (399 zero-claim), iaiyh 19/34. · Deferrals: populating sections[] for the 3 chapter-scheme PDF books + flipping any book to 'complete' happens during Phase G mining (the gate is the forcing function then); products flow unchanged — resume at the U-range.

The rule meant to slow animations down only capped how LONG each loop takes, never how MANY times it repeats — so a 10-second loop set to 0.01 seconds did not stop, it ran a hundred times a second. Seven things on screen were strobing. One line fixed it, and a new probe makes the bug impossible to reintroduce. · CAUSE: design-system.css:307-318's `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` set `animation-duration: 0.01s !important` + `transition-duration: 0.01s !important` and never set `animation-iteration-count`. Capping duration does not stop an `infinite` animation — it ACCELERATES it by 1000x. MEASURED headless with the media feature emulated (puppeteer, emulateMediaFeatures prefers-reduced-motion=reduce): 7 PAINTED offenders at ~100Hz — ds-scan-sweep (.ds-scan-line, the worst: ramps opacity 0->0.35 while sweeping top -3%->103% across .essentials-host), ds-numeric-glow (.coverage-stat__num, the hero 13/90), ds-stat-pulse (.coverage-stat::before), ds-travel-top + ds-travel-bottom (.coverage-hero::before/::after), and ds-pulse-animate x2 (.topbar__ask-dot + .topbar__workspace-tag::before). WCAG 2.3.1 draws the flash line at 3/sec. The severity ranks honestly: the scan-line is a genuine flash hazard (position + opacity over a large host); the others are luminance shimmers on small or soft elements — real, unintended, not the same class. · FIX: one declaration, `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`, inside the same reduced-motion block (design-system.css, SEALED — user sign-off: Luneth 2026-07-14 "1.
